newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S TRADE DEFICIT NARROWS TO $36 MLN IN MAY.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S TRADE DEFICIT NARROWS TO $36 MLN IN MAY.

text.p: Romania's trade balance
deficit narrowed to $36 million in May from $94.3 million the
previous month, as exports recovered and imports fell further,
National Statistics Board (CNS) data showed on Tuesday.
ROMANIAN TRADE MAY 97 APRIL 97 MAY 96
Exports million USD 716.2 700.0(676.3) n.a.(622.0)
(JANUARY TO MONTH)
Exports million USD 3,358.5 n.a.(2,617.2) n.a.(2,657.0)
NOTES -- Previous data in brackets. All figures in FOB
prices. The CNS said five-month imports this year included
$79.6 million of oil imports on which customs documents were
delayed. The 1997 data are subject to revisions.
Exports rose by 2.3 percent to $716.2 million in May from
the previous month, while imports saw a 5.3 percent fall to
$752.2 million, CNS data showed.
It said exports were 0.3 percent up to $3.36 billion over
January-May from the equivalent period of 1996, with textiles
and steel products topping the export list.
Five-month imports dropped by 10.5 percent from the same
period of 1996, helping the trade deficit to shrink to $339.9
million over January-May from $783.1 million a year ago.
The private sector accounted for 53.4 pecent of exports and
50.1 percent of imports over January-May.
Italy took the bulk of Romanian exports over January-May,
when Germany provided most of Romania's imports.
The CNS also said Romania's imports from Japan rose sharply
in May, amounting to $70.8 million compared with only $19.6
million in the first four months of this year.
-- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
